name: Techtronic Industries
lede: TTI is expanding in EMEA, Latin America and Asia while running cost programmes at RYOBI, Hoover and Vax and adapting its manufacturing footprint to tariffs. A connected layer gives every initiative one shared view.
why_h2: Growth and discipline at the same time
why_p: Record first-half results, a higher free cash flow target and multi-brand cost programmes all depend on initiatives being tracked consistently across regions and brands.

signals.title: Record H1 2026
signals.body: Revenue rose 5.9 percent to US$8.3 billion and net profit rose 17.5 percent to US$738 million, with an EBIT margin of 9.9 percent and a 20 percent higher interim dividend.
signals.angle: Regional expansion initiatives tracked against group targets in one place.

signals.title: Free cash flow target lifted
signals.body: TTI lifted its 2026 free cash flow target to about US$1.3 billion. The Milwaukee-anchored Professional segment reached US$5.9 billion in H1 sales, and cost reduction programmes continue at RYOBI, Hoover and Vax.
signals.angle: Initiative status, savings tracking and approvals consolidated across brands and sites for group reporting.

signals.title: Board updated
signals.body: The board composition was updated from 9 March 2026, with Horst Julius Pudwill as executive chairman, Stephan Horst Pudwill as executive vice chairman and Steven Philip Richman as CEO.
signals.angle: Standardised executive reporting cadences and operating reviews across the group.

signals.title: Record 2025 despite tariffs
signals.body: 2025 sales reached a record US$15.3 billion, up 4.4 percent, with Milwaukee up 7.9 percent and RYOBI up 5.4 percent in local currency. Management cites eight years of diversifying its manufacturing footprint.
signals.angle: Supplier, SKU and landed-cost changes across factories and brands managed in one connected system.
